correctness.rationale: The channel produces exactly the receiver sets defined by one zero-error or one valid decrement. Disjointness is equivalent to binary set packing with 243 receiver constraints; alternatively to independence in its 1890-edge confusability graph. Both separately constructed mixed-integer optimizations returned status optimal and a matching primal=dual cardinality of 45 with zero mixed-integer gap. The provided 45-word code was separately checked receiver by receiver (185 distinct received words). Solver correctness is an explicit dependency, and finite optimization is not a symbolic all-parameter theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete Section V.A and Table V of Fazeli–Vardy–Yaakobi (arXiv:1401.6496v1) establish only the finite fractional-packing bound 55, not the integer maximum 45. The full two-page Buzaglo–Etzion preprint concerns lattice and perfect codes, particularly n-1 and n-2 errors, not the unrestricted five-cell optimum. Exact-claim, channel-alias, and related published-finding corpus searches returned no statement implying the 45 optimum. Code-construction papers not fully accessed remain a bibliographic risk, not a demonstration of coverage. The claim of originality concerns closing the specific 55-to-45 integer optimum gap, not inventing the channel or the packing method.

value.rationale: The unrestricted exact number of messages storable with guaranteed recovery after one cell-level decrement is a natural finite capacity invariant; the foundational same-channel 2014 paper tabulates an upper bound 55 for precisely five ternary cells but leaves the integer optimum open. The 45-word explicit design and sharp upper bound close a ten-codeword finite gap, with relevance for evaluating nonlinear alternatives and moderate cell arrays. This is not claimed to establish a general family or physical implementation.
